poolName: VPC & Network Connectivity: Subnets, Routing, SGs/NACLs, NAT, Endpoints, Peering, Transit Gateway, VPN & Direct Connect (Mixed Difficulty)
description: SAA-C03 revision questions on Amazon VPC at Easy, Medium and Hard difficulty: subnets and routing, security groups and NACLs, internet/NAT/egress-only gateways, VPC endpoints and PrivateLink, peering and Transit Gateway, Site-to-Site and Client VPN, Direct Connect, VPC Lattice, Flow Logs, Traffic Mirroring and Network Firewall.

questions.prompt: What is the scope of a VPC and of the subnets inside it?
choices: A VPC spans all Regions, and each subnet spans all Availability Zones
A VPC spans every Availability Zone in a Region, and each subnet spans multiple Regions
A VPC is tied to one Availability Zone, and each subnet spans the whole Region
A VPC is tied to one Region, and each subnet is created in a single Availability Zone
questions.correctChoice: A VPC is tied to one Region, and each subnet is created in a single Availability Zone
questions.explanation: VPCs are regional and cannot span Regions (use peering or similar to connect them). A VPC covers the Availability Zones of its Region, but each subnet lives in exactly one AZ.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the default VPC in an AWS Region is correct?
choices: It cannot be deleted, so every Region always keeps exactly one
It uses the 172.31.0.0/16 IPv4 CIDR, has a subnet in each AZ, and comes with an internet gateway and a route to it
It uses the 10.0.0.0/16 IPv4 CIDR and has only private subnets, with no route to the internet
It is created only in the account's first Region and has one subnet spanning all AZs
questions.correctChoice: It uses the 172.31.0.0/16 IPv4 CIDR, has a subnet in each AZ, and comes with an internet gateway and a route to it
questions.explanation: The default VPC comes with a 172.31.0.0/16 CIDR, one default subnet per AZ, an IGW, a default SG, NACL, DHCP options set and a route table with a route out via the IGW. It can be deleted and recreated.

questions.prompt: Which VPC component incurs hourly and data-processing charges?
choices: An internet gateway
A NAT gateway
A route table
A security group
questions.correctChoice: A NAT gateway
questions.explanation: NAT gateways are billed per hour and per GB processed. VPCs, subnets, route tables, NACLs, security groups and internet gateways have no charge themselves.

questions.prompt: EC2 instances in private subnets download several terabytes a month from Amazon S3 through a NAT gateway, and the NAT data-processing charges are high. The traffic must stay off the public internet. What is the most cost-effective change?
choices: Create an S3 gateway endpoint and add it to the private subnets' route tables
Create an S3 interface endpoint and keep the NAT gateway as a fallback route
Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance
Add an internet gateway and assign Elastic IP addresses to the instances
questions.correctChoice: Create an S3 gateway endpoint and add it to the private subnets' route tables
questions.explanation: Gateway endpoints for S3 (and DynamoDB) have no hourly or data-processing charge and keep traffic on the AWS network. Interface endpoints and NAT gateways are billed per hour and per GB.

questions.prompt: Which pair of services is supported by VPC gateway endpoints?
choices: AWS Lambda and Amazon CloudWatch
Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS
Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS
questions.correctChoice: Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB
questions.explanation: Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB. Other AWS services are reached privately with interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink).

questions.prompt: How does an interface VPC endpoint provide private access to a supported service?
choices: It adds a route-table entry that points to a managed prefix list for the service
It creates a VPN tunnel between the VPC and the service
It assigns a public IP address to each instance so traffic can use the internet gateway
It places elastic network interfaces with private IP addresses in your subnets, powered by AWS PrivateLink
questions.correctChoice: It places elastic network interfaces with private IP addresses in your subnets, powered by AWS PrivateLink
questions.explanation: Interface endpoints are ENIs with private IPs that act as the entry point to a PrivateLink-powered service. Gateway endpoints are the type that works through route-table entries.

questions.prompt: A new custom VPC has an internet gateway attached. An EC2 instance in one subnet has a public IPv4 address and a security group that allows inbound HTTP, but it is unreachable from the internet. What is the most likely missing configuration?
choices: An outbound security group rule that allows HTTP responses
A virtual private gateway attached to the VPC
A 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway in the subnet's route table
A NAT gateway in the same subnet
questions.correctChoice: A 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway in the subnet's route table
questions.explanation: Attaching an IGW is not enough; the subnet's route table needs a default route targeting it. Security groups are stateful, so no outbound rule is needed for responses.

questions.prompt: What does the destination 0.0.0.0/0 in a route table represent?
choices: Only private RFC 1918 address ranges used inside the VPC
All possible IPv6 addresses (the IPv6 default route)
All possible IPv4 addresses (the catch-all or default route)
Only addresses inside the VPC's own IPv4 CIDR block (the local range)
questions.correctChoice: All possible IPv4 addresses (the catch-all or default route)
questions.explanation: 0.0.0.0/0 matches every IPv4 address; ::/0 is the IPv6 equivalent. A route to an IGW or NAT gateway on this destination sends all non-local traffic there.

questions.prompt: A networking account wants other accounts in the same AWS Organization to launch resources into its VPC. What does VPC sharing with AWS RAM actually share?
choices: The entire VPC including its security groups
Internet gateways only
Subnets
Route tables only
questions.correctChoice: Subnets
questions.explanation: VPC sharing shares subnets (via a RAM resource share) with accounts in the same organization. Default subnets cannot be shared.

questions.prompt: A production VPC is running out of private IPv4 addresses. The team wants to add capacity without rebuilding the VPC or moving existing workloads. What should they do?
choices: Associate an additional (secondary) IPv4 CIDR block with the VPC and create new subnets in it
Delete and recreate the VPC with a larger primary CIDR block
Create a second VPC with the same CIDR range and peer it with the first VPC
Resize the CIDR blocks of the existing subnets to make them larger
questions.correctChoice: Associate an additional (secondary) IPv4 CIDR block with the VPC and create new subnets in it
questions.explanation: A VPC can have multiple IPv4 CIDR blocks (quota adjustable), so you can associate another block and add subnets from it. Existing subnet CIDRs cannot be changed, and overlapping ranges break routing between VPCs.

questions.prompt: A security group allows inbound TCP 443 and has no outbound rules that match the reply traffic. What happens to the responses sent by the instance?
choices: They are allowed automatically because security groups are stateful
They are allowed only if the subnet's NACL has an outbound allow rule
They are dropped because security groups only evaluate inbound traffic
They are blocked until an outbound rule for the ephemeral ports is added
questions.correctChoice: They are allowed automatically because security groups are stateful
questions.explanation: Security groups track connection state, so replies to allowed inbound requests are returned regardless of outbound rules. (A NACL could still block them, but the stem asks about the security group.)

questions.prompt: How many network ACLs can a subnet be associated with at one time?
choices: None; NACLs attach to instances, not subnets
Exactly one
Any number, evaluated together
Up to five
questions.correctChoice: Exactly one
questions.explanation: Each subnet is associated with exactly one NACL, while one NACL can be associated with many subnets in the same VPC.

questions.prompt: A team needs to explicitly deny traffic from a specific malicious IP address range to a subnet. Which feature supports an explicit deny rule?
choices: A route table
A network ACL
A security group
An Elastic IP address
questions.correctChoice: A network ACL
questions.explanation: NACLs support both allow and deny rules. Security groups only contain allow rules.

questions.prompt: A subnet's inbound NACL has rule 90 DENY TCP 443 from 203.0.113.0/24 and rule 100 ALLOW TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. What happens to an HTTPS request from 203.0.113.25?
choices: It is denied only if the security group also denies it
It is allowed because the higher-numbered allow rule overrides a deny rule
It is allowed because allow rules always take precedence over deny rules
It is denied because the lower-numbered rule 90 is evaluated first and matches
questions.correctChoice: It is denied because the lower-numbered rule 90 is evaluated first and matches
questions.explanation: NACL rules are evaluated in ascending rule-number order and the first match is applied. Rule 90 matches first, so the request is denied.

questions.prompt: A web server in a public subnet is reachable on HTTPS until the team associates a new custom NACL with an inbound rule allowing TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Clients now time out. What is missing?
choices: An inbound NACL rule allowing ICMP so clients can test the path
An outbound security group rule allowing TCP 443 to the clients
A second NACL associated with the subnet for the return path
An outbound rule for the clients' ephemeral ports, as NACLs are stateless
questions.correctChoice: An outbound rule for the clients' ephemeral ports, as NACLs are stateless
questions.explanation: NACLs do not track connection state, so return traffic must be explicitly allowed by an outbound rule covering the client's ephemeral port range.

questions.prompt: An application tier must accept traffic only from instances in the web tier, which scale in and out and change IP addresses frequently. How should the application tier's security group be configured?
choices: Allow inbound traffic from the web subnet's CIDR block in the NACL only
Allow inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 and rely on the OS firewall
Assign Elastic IP addresses to the web tier and allow those addresses
Allow inbound traffic with the web tier's security group as the source
questions.correctChoice: Allow inbound traffic with the web tier's security group as the source
questions.explanation: Security group rules can reference another security group, so membership rather than IP addresses defines who is allowed. It tracks scaling automatically.

questions.prompt: An engineer creates a new custom NACL, associates it with a working subnet and adds no rules. What is the effect on traffic in that subnet?
choices: All traffic is allowed, as with the default NACL
Traffic is controlled by the security groups alone because the NACL has no rules
All inbound and outbound traffic is denied until allow rules are added
Only inbound traffic is denied
questions.correctChoice: All inbound and outbound traffic is denied until allow rules are added
questions.explanation: The default NACL allows all traffic, but a newly created custom NACL denies everything (including the implicit final * deny rule) until you add rules.

questions.prompt: A subnet's NACL has an inbound rule 100 allowing TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. The security team must block one abusive /24 range from reaching every instance in the subnet while keeping HTTPS open to everyone else. Which action meets the requirement?
choices: Add an inbound NACL DENY rule for that range with a rule number lower than 100
Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 allow from the NACL and rely on the security group
Add an inbound NACL DENY rule for that range with a rule number higher than 100
Add a deny rule for that range to the instances' security group
questions.correctChoice: Add an inbound NACL DENY rule for that range with a rule number lower than 100
questions.explanation: Only NACLs can deny, and they are evaluated lowest number first. A deny numbered above 100 would never be reached for HTTPS traffic because rule 100 matches first. Security groups have no deny rules.

questions.prompt: What is the traffic behaviour of a newly created custom security group that has had no rules edited?
choices: All inbound and all outbound traffic is allowed
All inbound and all outbound traffic is denied
All inbound traffic is allowed and all outbound traffic is denied
All inbound traffic is denied and all outbound traffic is allowed
questions.correctChoice: All inbound traffic is denied and all outbound traffic is allowed
questions.explanation: Security groups are allow-list only. A new custom group has no inbound rules (implicit deny) and a default rule allowing all outbound traffic.

questions.prompt: Which statement about associating a single security group with instances is correct?
choices: It can only be used by instances in one subnet
It can only be associated with one instance at a time
It can be used by instances in different subnets of the same VPC
It can be used by instances in any VPC in the same Region
questions.correctChoice: It can be used by instances in different subnets of the same VPC
questions.explanation: Security groups operate at the instance (ENI) level, are not tied to a subnet or AZ, but are scoped to a single VPC.

questions.prompt: Instances in a private subnet need to download OS patches from the internet but must not accept unsolicited inbound connections from the internet. Which component should be used?
choices: An egress-only internet gateway
A NAT gateway
A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint
A virtual private gateway
questions.correctChoice: A NAT gateway
questions.explanation: A NAT gateway lets private IPv4 instances initiate outbound connections and does not allow unsolicited inbound connections. An egress-only IGW does the equivalent only for IPv6.

questions.prompt: Where should a zonal public NAT gateway be placed, and what must private subnets do to use it?
choices: In a private subnet; public subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 to it
In the same private subnet as the instances; no route change is needed
In a public subnet; private subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway
In a public subnet with an Elastic IP; private subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 to it
questions.correctChoice: In a public subnet with an Elastic IP; private subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 to it
questions.explanation: A public NAT gateway needs an Elastic IP and sits in a public subnet (route to an IGW). Private subnets send their default route to the NAT gateway.

questions.prompt: A workload runs in private subnets across three AZs and uses a single zonal NAT gateway in one AZ. During an outage of that AZ, instances in the other AZs lose outbound internet access. What is the best design to improve availability?
choices: Deploy a NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet to its own AZ's NAT gateway
Keep one NAT gateway and attach a second Elastic IP address to it for redundancy
Move the NAT gateway to a private subnet in a different AZ
Add a second route table entry in each private subnet pointing to the same NAT gateway
questions.correctChoice: Deploy a NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet to its own AZ's NAT gateway
questions.explanation: A zonal NAT gateway is confined to one AZ, so the recommended pattern is one per AZ with AZ-local routing. This also avoids cross-AZ data charges.

questions.prompt: Which gateway allows instances with IPv6 addresses to initiate outbound internet connections while preventing the internet from initiating connections to them?
choices: A virtual private gateway
An egress-only internet gateway
A NAT gateway
An internet gateway
questions.correctChoice: An egress-only internet gateway
questions.explanation: The egress-only internet gateway is the IPv6 equivalent of a NAT gateway for outbound-only access. A standard IGW would allow inbound connections too.

questions.prompt: A partner has allow-listed the public IPv4 address of an EC2 instance, but the address changes every time the instance is stopped and started. What should be used?
choices: An Elastic IP address associated with the instance
An egress-only internet gateway
A larger instance type with a public subnet
A second ENI with a private IP address
questions.correctChoice: An Elastic IP address associated with the instance
questions.explanation: An Elastic IP is a static public IPv4 address that remains the same across restarts and can be remapped to another instance or ENI.

questions.prompt: A route table contains: 10.0.0.0/16 -> local; 0.0.0.0/0 -> igw; 192.168.0.0/16 -> vgw; 192.168.10.0/24 -> tgw. Where is traffic destined for 192.168.10.5 sent?
choices: To the transit gateway, because the most specific matching route wins
To the virtual private gateway, because it was added first
To the local target, because it has the highest priority
To the internet gateway, because 0.0.0.0/0 is the default route
questions.correctChoice: To the transit gateway, because the most specific matching route wins
questions.explanation: Route selection uses the longest prefix match. 192.168.10.0/24 is more specific than 192.168.0.0/16 and 0.0.0.0/0.

questions.prompt: A new subnet is created in a VPC without any explicit route table association. Which route table does it use?
choices: No route table; it can only communicate within the subnet
The VPC's main (default) route table
The route table of the nearest subnet in the same AZ
A new empty route table created for the subnet
questions.correctChoice: The VPC's main (default) route table
questions.explanation: Subnets without an explicit association implicitly use the main route table, which can't be deleted. A subnet is associated with only one route table at a time.

questions.prompt: A team added a default route to an internet gateway in the VPC's main route table. Later, new subnets created for databases unexpectedly became public. What is the best practice to prevent this?
choices: Change the main route table's default route target from the IGW to a NAT gateway
Add a deny entry for 0.0.0.0/0 to the main route table for database subnets
Keep the main route table private and explicitly associate public subnets with a custom route table holding the IGW route
Delete the main route table so each subnet must be associated explicitly
questions.correctChoice: Keep the main route table private and explicitly associate public subnets with a custom route table holding the IGW route
questions.explanation: New subnets default to the main route table, so a public main route table makes every new subnet public. Use explicit associations for public subnets instead.

questions.prompt: An IPv4-only VPC must be updated so instances can also communicate over IPv6. Which set of actions is required?
choices: Add IPv6 CIDRs to the VPC and subnets, route ::/0 to the IGW, update security group rules for IPv6 and use IPv6-capable instance types
Create a new IPv6-only VPC, peer it with the old VPC and move the IPv4 addresses to it
Replace the internet gateway with a NAT gateway so that IPv6 addresses are translated to IPv4
Disable IPv4 on the VPC first, then enable IPv6 on the existing subnets
questions.correctChoice: Add IPv6 CIDRs to the VPC and subnets, route ::/0 to the IGW, update security group rules for IPv6 and use IPv6-capable instance types
questions.explanation: Dual-stack requires adding IPv6 CIDRs, routing IPv6 (::/0) to the IGW, allowing IPv6 in SG/NACL rules and using instance types that support IPv6. IPv4 cannot be disabled on a VPC.

questions.prompt: Workloads in private subnets must reach an on-premises system over a Site-to-Site VPN attached to a transit gateway. The on-premises firewall allows traffic only from one approved private IP. Which solution satisfies this?
choices: An egress-only internet gateway in the VPC, with the on-premises firewall allowing the VPC's IPv6 range
A private NAT gateway routed through the transit gateway, translating sources to its own private IP
A public NAT gateway with an Elastic IP in a public subnet, with the on-premises firewall allowing that address
An interface VPC endpoint that targets the on-premises system's private IP address
questions.correctChoice: A private NAT gateway routed through the transit gateway, translating sources to its own private IP
questions.explanation: Private NAT gateways connect private subnets to other VPCs or on-premises networks through a transit gateway or virtual private gateway and cannot have an Elastic IP. Public NAT gateways are for internet access.

questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of a NAT gateway over a self-managed NAT instance?
choices: It accepts unsolicited inbound connections from the internet to private instances
It is managed, so there is no instance to patch or size
It can also double as a bastion host for SSH access to private instances
It has no hourly or data-processing charge compared with an instance
questions.correctChoice: It is managed, so there is no instance to patch or size
questions.explanation: NAT gateways are AWS-managed and recommended over NAT instances, which require you to handle scaling, patching and disabling the source/destination check. NAT gateways are billed and cannot act as bastions.

questions.prompt: Administrators need shell access to EC2 instances in private subnets. Security policy forbids opening inbound SSH from the internet and the team wants to avoid operating bastion hosts. Which option fits best?
choices: An Elastic IP address on each private instance
A NAT gateway with an inbound rule allowing port 22
An additional internet gateway attached to the VPC
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
questions.correctChoice: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
questions.explanation: Session Manager provides access without inbound ports, public IPs or bastions. NAT gateways are for outbound access only and cannot be used as bastions.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a bastion host (jump box) in a VPC?
choices: A managed service that translates private IPv4 addresses for outbound internet access
A hosted connection that links on-premises networks to AWS
A hardened instance that provides controlled administrative access, such as SSH, into private subnets
A gateway that distributes traffic to third-party firewall appliances
questions.correctChoice: A hardened instance that provides controlled administrative access, such as SSH, into private subnets
questions.explanation: A bastion is a security-hardened VM that acts as the entry point for admin access to private resources. AWS has no managed bastion; Session Manager or EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint can replace it.

questions.prompt: Which statement about charges for public IPv4 addresses is correct?
choices: Only Elastic IPs that are not associated with a running instance are charged
Public IPv4 addresses are free; only NAT gateways are charged for them
Public IPv4 addresses are free while attached to a running instance and charged only when released
Every public IPv4 address, including Elastic IPs that are idle, is charged per hour
questions.correctChoice: Every public IPv4 address, including Elastic IPs that are idle, is charged per hour
questions.explanation: AWS charges per hour for all public IPv4 addresses, whether in use or idle. This encourages IPv6 adoption and releasing unused addresses.

questions.prompt: Application servers in private subnets make very high volumes of outbound calls to internet APIs that support IPv6. NAT gateway data-processing charges are significant, and the servers must not accept inbound connections from the internet. What should the architect do to reduce cost?
choices: Replace each NAT gateway with an interface VPC endpoint for the APIs
Enable IPv6 on the VPC and subnets and route ::/0 to an egress-only internet gateway
Route ::/0 to an internet gateway
Add a second NAT gateway per AZ to spread the data processing
questions.correctChoice: Enable IPv6 on the VPC and subnets and route ::/0 to an egress-only internet gateway
questions.explanation: An egress-only internet gateway gives outbound-only IPv6 access with no hourly or data-processing charge. An IGW would also allow inbound connections, and additional NAT gateways increase cost.

questions.prompt: A VPC subnet is shared with a participant account through AWS RAM. What can the participant account do?
choices: Modify the shared subnet's route tables and NACLs to suit its workloads
View and manage all resources created by other participants in the shared subnet
Create and manage its own resources, such as EC2 instances, in the shared subnet but not the owner's route tables or others' resources
Delete the shared subnet and attach its own internet gateway to the VPC
questions.correctChoice: Create and manage its own resources, such as EC2 instances, in the shared subnet but not the owner's route tables or others' resources
questions.explanation: The VPC owner manages subnets, route tables, NACLs and gateways. Participants can only see and manage their own resources in the shared subnet.

questions.prompt: A public NAT gateway with an Elastic IP was created and the private subnet's route table has 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gateway. The private instances still cannot reach the internet. The NAT gateway's subnet is associated with a route table that has only the local route. What is the problem?
choices: The NAT gateway must be placed in the same subnet as the instances
The NAT gateway's subnet has no route to an internet gateway, so it must be moved to a public subnet
The NAT gateway needs a virtual private gateway attached to the VPC
The private instances need public IPv4 addresses for the NAT gateway to translate
questions.correctChoice: The NAT gateway's subnet has no route to an internet gateway, so it must be moved to a public subnet
questions.explanation: A public NAT gateway reaches the internet through an IGW, so its own subnet needs a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the IGW. Instances behind NAT use private IPs only.

questions.prompt: A web application must be highly available across two AZs. Users reach it over the internet through a load balancer. The application servers need outbound internet access for updates, and the database must have no internet path at all. Which subnet design meets these requirements?
choices: Load balancer in private subnets with a NAT gateway providing inbound access for users
Load balancer, application servers and database all in public subnets with security groups
Load balancer in public subnets, application servers in private subnets with a NAT gateway per AZ, and database in private subnets with no default route
Load balancer in public subnets, application servers and database in private subnets sharing one NAT gateway route for all tiers
questions.correctChoice: Load balancer in public subnets, application servers in private subnets with a NAT gateway per AZ, and database in private subnets with no default route
questions.explanation: Public subnets host internet-facing entry points, private app subnets reach the internet via NAT (one per AZ for resilience), and database subnets have no default route. NAT gateways cannot provide inbound access.

questions.prompt: A licence server is bound to a specific private IP address and Elastic IP. If the instance fails, a standby instance must take over the same addresses quickly. Which approach works?
choices: Associate a second NACL with the subnet that allows the standby's addresses
Move the ENI holding the addresses to the standby (or remap the Elastic IP)
Launch the standby in another Region and connect it to the VPC using VPC peering
Create a new subnet in the same AZ with the same CIDR range and move the standby there
questions.correctChoice: Move the ENI holding the addresses to the standby (or remap the Elastic IP)
questions.explanation: ENIs and Elastic IPs can be moved between instances, so a standby can take over fixed IP addresses without clients changing configuration.

questions.prompt: What is an elastic network interface (ENI)?
choices: A dedicated physical connection from a data centre to AWS
A managed virtual router that connects multiple VPCs and on-premises networks
A virtual network card in a VPC that attaches to compute resources
A stateless firewall that filters traffic at the subnet level
questions.correctChoice: A virtual network card in a VPC that attaches to compute resources
questions.explanation: ENIs are virtual network cards with IP addresses used by EC2 and other compute types. They are also the basis of interface endpoints and transit gateway attachments.

questions.prompt: VPC A is peered with VPC B, and VPC B is peered with VPC C. Can instances in VPC A reach instances in VPC C through VPC B?
choices: Yes, because peering relationships are automatically shared
No, because VPC peering is not transitive
Yes, if the route tables in VPC B allow it
Only if all three VPCs are in the same account
questions.correctChoice: No, because VPC peering is not transitive
questions.explanation: VPC peering is a one-to-one relationship with no transitive routing. Connect A and C directly, or use a transit gateway.

questions.prompt: Which condition prevents two VPCs from being peered?
choices: Their CIDR blocks overlap
One of them uses IPv6 and the other IPv4
They are in different AWS accounts
They are in different Regions
questions.correctChoice: Their CIDR blocks overlap
questions.explanation: Peered VPCs must have non-overlapping CIDR blocks. Peering works across accounts and Regions.

questions.prompt: A peering connection between two VPCs shows as active, yet instances cannot reach each other using private IPs. Security groups and NACLs allow the traffic. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The peering connection needs an internet gateway attached to each VPC
The VPCs need a transit gateway attachment for each subnet to forward the traffic
The peering connection requires a NAT gateway in each VPC to translate addresses
Routes to the peer's CIDR via the peering connection are missing from the route tables
questions.correctChoice: Routes to the peer's CIDR via the peering connection are missing from the route tables
questions.explanation: After creating and accepting the peering connection, you must add routes in the route table of each VPC targeting the peering connection.

questions.prompt: A VPC in us-east-1 is peered with a VPC in eu-west-1. How can the security group in us-east-1 allow traffic from the instances in eu-west-1?
choices: Attach the eu-west-1 security group to the us-east-1 instances through the peering connection
Use the peer VPC's CIDR range as the source, as SG references across peering work only within a Region
Reference the eu-west-1 security group ID as the source in the inbound rule
Reference the eu-west-1 security group by name in an outbound rule on the us-east-1 group
questions.correctChoice: Use the peer VPC's CIDR range as the source, as SG references across peering work only within a Region
questions.explanation: A security group rule can reference a peer VPC's security group only for same-Region peering. For inter-Region peering, use CIDR ranges.

questions.prompt: Which statement about VPC peering is correct?
choices: It supports transitive routing when a central hub VPC is used
It works only within one Region and the connection itself is billed hourly
It relies on separate hardware and can become a bandwidth bottleneck
It can link VPCs across accounts and Regions; cross-AZ or cross-Region data transfer is charged
questions.correctChoice: It can link VPCs across accounts and Regions; cross-AZ or cross-Region data transfer is charged
questions.explanation: Peering supports cross-account and inter-Region connections, has no single point of failure or bandwidth bottleneck, and has no charge itself, but cross-AZ and cross-Region data transfer is billed.

questions.prompt: A company has 30 VPCs in one Region that must all communicate with each other and with an on-premises network via a Site-to-Site VPN. The team wants minimal ongoing operational overhead. Which solution is best?
choices: Attach all VPCs and the VPN to a transit gateway
Create a full mesh of VPC peering connections and a VPN for each VPC
Create a virtual private gateway in each VPC and connect them to each other
Peer all VPCs to one central VPC and route through it
questions.correctChoice: Attach all VPCs and the VPN to a transit gateway
questions.explanation: A transit gateway is a regional hub-and-spoke router for many VPCs and VPN/Direct Connect attachments. Peering is non-transitive, so a full mesh scales poorly (hundreds of connections and route entries).

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of AWS Transit Gateway?
choices: To act as a regional hub that interconnects many VPCs and on-premises networks
To provide private access to S3 and DynamoDB from a VPC
To provide a static public IPv4 address for instances
To filter traffic at the subnet level with allow and deny rules
questions.correctChoice: To act as a regional hub that interconnects many VPCs and on-premises networks
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway is a regional virtual router that connects VPCs, VPN and Direct Connect attachments in a hub-and-spoke model.

questions.prompt: A company has a transit gateway in us-east-1 connecting several VPCs and another in eu-west-1 connecting several more. The two groups of VPCs must communicate. What should they do?
choices: Attach the eu-west-1 VPCs directly to the us-east-1 transit gateway
Use a gateway endpoint in each Region
Create a transit gateway peering attachment between the two transit gateways
Create a virtual private gateway in each Region and connect them
questions.correctChoice: Create a transit gateway peering attachment between the two transit gateways
questions.explanation: Transit gateways are Regional resources, so cross-Region connectivity uses transit gateway peering.

questions.prompt: A security team requires all traffic between 15 VPCs, and between those VPCs and on-premises, to be inspected by third-party firewall appliances. The appliances must scale and be managed centrally. Which architecture fits?
choices: Peer every VPC with the inspection VPC and rely on transitive routing through it
Use VPC gateway endpoints in each VPC to reach the appliances
Deploy a NAT gateway in each VPC and send traffic through it to the appliances
Route VPC and on-premises traffic via a transit gateway to an inspection VPC with appliances behind a Gateway Load Balancer
questions.correctChoice: Route VPC and on-premises traffic via a transit gateway to an inspection VPC with appliances behind a Gateway Load Balancer
questions.explanation: A transit gateway centralises routing; appliances in an inspection VPC behind a GWLB scale and distribute flows. Peering is not transitive, and NAT gateways and gateway endpoints do not inspect traffic.

questions.prompt: VPC A is peered with VPC B, and VPC B has a Site-to-Site VPN to the corporate network. Instances in VPC A cannot reach on-premises resources through VPC B even though routes were added. What is the correct fix?
choices: Add a second peering connection between VPC A and VPC B for the on-premises traffic
Enable transitive routing on the peering connection and add a route to the on-premises CIDR
Attach both VPCs and the VPN to a transit gateway, as peering cannot forward traffic to B's VPN connection
Associate VPC B's virtual private gateway with VPC A's route table and add the on-premises CIDR
questions.correctChoice: Attach both VPCs and the VPN to a transit gateway, as peering cannot forward traffic to B's VPN connection
questions.explanation: Peering does not support transitive (edge-to-edge) routing through the peer's VPN, so traffic from A cannot use B's gateways. A transit gateway provides this hub connectivity.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of a VPC endpoint?
choices: It provides a static public IP address for outbound traffic from private subnets
It connects two VPCs, including those that have overlapping CIDR blocks, over the AWS network
Instances without public IPs reach supported AWS services privately, without an IGW, NAT, VPN or Direct Connect
It encrypts all traffic between a VPC and an on-premises network using IPsec
questions.correctChoice: Instances without public IPs reach supported AWS services privately, without an IGW, NAT, VPN or Direct Connect
questions.explanation: VPC endpoints keep traffic on the AWS network and remove the need for IGW, NAT, VPN or Direct Connect to reach supported services.

questions.prompt: Application servers in a VPC with no internet gateway or NAT must send messages to Amazon SQS. Which solution provides private connectivity?
choices: An egress-only internet gateway
A gateway VPC endpoint for SQS
An interface VPC endpoint for SQS
A VPC peering connection to the SQS service
questions.correctChoice: An interface VPC endpoint for SQS
questions.explanation: Gateway endpoints support only S3 and DynamoDB. Most other services, including SQS, are reached privately via interface endpoints (PrivateLink).

questions.prompt: An on-premises application accesses Amazon S3 over an existing Direct Connect connection and the security team wants the traffic to use private IP addresses rather than public S3 endpoints. Which solution fits?
choices: Create a NAT gateway in the VPC and route on-premises traffic to S3 through it
Create an S3 interface endpoint and have on-premises clients use its private IP addresses
Create an S3 gateway endpoint and attach it to the Direct Connect gateway for on-premises access
Create an S3 gateway endpoint in the VPC and route on-premises traffic to it
questions.correctChoice: Create an S3 interface endpoint and have on-premises clients use its private IP addresses
questions.explanation: Gateway endpoints are used through VPC route tables and cannot be extended to on-premises networks. S3 interface endpoints have private IPs that are reachable over Direct Connect or VPN.

questions.prompt: A team creates an S3 gateway endpoint, but instances in a private subnet still send S3 traffic through the NAT gateway. What should they check?
choices: That the endpoint is associated with the private subnet's route table
That a second internet gateway is attached to the VPC for S3 traffic
That an Elastic IP address is attached to the endpoint
That the endpoint was created inside a public subnet
questions.correctChoice: That the endpoint is associated with the private subnet's route table
questions.explanation: Gateway endpoints work through route-table entries, so the endpoint must be associated with the route tables of the subnets that should use it.

questions.prompt: A SaaS provider hosts its service in its own VPC and must give hundreds of customer VPCs private access to it. Customers use overlapping CIDR ranges, and the provider does not want customers to reach anything else in its VPC. Which solution should the provider use?
choices: Give each customer a Site-to-Site VPN connection into the provider's VPC over the internet
Attach every customer VPC to a transit gateway owned by the provider and share it through RAM
Create a VPC peering connection between the provider VPC and each customer VPC
Put the service behind a Network Load Balancer as a PrivateLink endpoint service that customers reach through interface endpoints
questions.correctChoice: Put the service behind a Network Load Balancer as a PrivateLink endpoint service that customers reach through interface endpoints
questions.explanation: PrivateLink exposes a single service to consumers, works with overlapping CIDRs and does not expose the rest of the provider VPC. Peering and transit gateways need non-overlapping CIDRs and give network-level access.

questions.prompt: Which service is designed to deploy, scale and manage a fleet of third-party virtual appliances, such as firewalls, in the network path?
choices: Gateway Load Balancer
AWS Storage Gateway
Amazon API Gateway
Application Load Balancer
questions.correctChoice: Gateway Load Balancer
questions.explanation: A Gateway Load Balancer operates at the network layer (layer 3) and distributes traffic to virtual appliances such as firewalls and intrusion detection/prevention systems.

questions.prompt: A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint has been created in an application VPC. How is traffic sent to the appliances behind the Gateway Load Balancer?
choices: Route table entries use the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint as the target
Security group rules redirect traffic to the endpoint
The NACL is configured to forward packets to the appliances
The application's DNS records are updated to the appliance IP addresses
questions.correctChoice: Route table entries use the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint as the target
questions.explanation: Traffic reaches the GWLB endpoint through route table changes; the endpoint sends it over PrivateLink to the GWLB, which distributes it to the appliances and returns it.

questions.prompt: Microservices run in dozens of VPCs across several accounts, some with overlapping CIDR blocks. The team wants IAM-based authorisation per service, HTTPS between services, and weighted routing for canary releases, without managing peering or transit routing. Which service should they use?
choices: AWS Transit Gateway with a shared route table
Amazon VPC Lattice
VPC peering with security group references
A Gateway Load Balancer with a GWLB endpoint in each VPC
questions.correctChoice: Amazon VPC Lattice
questions.explanation: VPC Lattice is an application networking layer that connects services across VPCs and accounts, handles overlapping addressing, integrates with IAM and supports weighted routing. Transit gateways and peering are network-level and require non-overlapping CIDRs.

questions.prompt: What is Amazon VPC Lattice?
choices: A managed application networking service that connects, secures and monitors services across VPCs and accounts
A service that mirrors network traffic from ENIs to security monitoring appliances
A dedicated physical connection from on-premises to AWS through a Direct Connect location
A managed firewall that performs deep packet inspection at the VPC perimeter using Suricata rules
questions.correctChoice: A managed application networking service that connects, secures and monitors services across VPCs and accounts
questions.explanation: VPC Lattice provides service-to-service connectivity, authentication and observability for microservices without managing the underlying network plumbing.

questions.prompt: In VPC Lattice, which construct is the logical container that groups services so that associated VPCs can communicate with them?
choices: A listener
A resource share
A target group
A service network
questions.correctChoice: A service network
questions.explanation: A service network is the logical boundary for services; VPCs associated with it can reach its services. Target groups hold targets and listeners define protocol and port.

questions.prompt: A company wants to connect its branch office network to a VPC over the internet with encrypted tunnels, and have it running quickly at low cost. Which service fits?
choices: VPC peering
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Client VPN
questions.correctChoice: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
questions.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec tunnels over the internet to connect an on-premises network or branch office to a VPC. Client VPN is for individual users.

questions.prompt: In a Site-to-Site VPN, which component is the VPN endpoint on the Amazon side attached to a single VPC?
choices: The virtual private gateway
The egress-only internet gateway
The customer gateway
The customer gateway device
questions.correctChoice: The virtual private gateway
questions.explanation: The virtual private gateway is the AWS-side VPN endpoint attached to one VPC. The customer gateway is the AWS resource that describes your on-premises device (the customer gateway device).

questions.prompt: Why does AWS provide two tunnels for each Site-to-Site VPN connection?
choices: To separate IPv4 traffic from IPv6 traffic across the two tunnels
To keep production traffic and test traffic isolated from each other
For redundancy, because the tunnels terminate in different Availability Zones
To double throughput by automatically combining both tunnels into one
questions.correctChoice: For redundancy, because the tunnels terminate in different Availability Zones
questions.explanation: Each connection has two tunnels, each with its own endpoint in a different AZ, so connectivity survives an AZ or endpoint failure.

questions.prompt: A company needs to send IPv6 traffic between its data centre and its VPCs over a Site-to-Site VPN. How must the VPN be terminated?
choices: On a customer gateway with IPv6 enabled in its BGP ASN configuration
On a transit gateway, as a virtual private gateway does not carry IPv6 over Site-to-Site VPN
On a virtual private gateway with an ::/0 route to the VPN connection
On an internet gateway combined with an egress-only internet gateway
questions.correctChoice: On a transit gateway, as a virtual private gateway does not carry IPv6 over Site-to-Site VPN
questions.explanation: IPv6 traffic is not supported on a Site-to-Site VPN that terminates on a virtual private gateway; a transit gateway attachment is required.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service lets individual remote users securely connect from their laptops to resources in a VPC using an OpenVPN-based client?
choices: AWS Transit Gateway
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Client VPN
questions.correctChoice: AWS Client VPN
questions.explanation: Client VPN is a managed client-based VPN for users. Site-to-Site VPN connects whole networks.

questions.prompt: Remote developers must reach a database in a private subnet using their corporate SSO credentials, with no public exposure of the database. Which solution meets this?
choices: An egress-only internet gateway
A NAT gateway with a security group allowing the developers' IP addresses
AWS Site-to-Site VPN with a customer gateway on each laptop
AWS Client VPN with federated (SAML) authentication
questions.correctChoice: AWS Client VPN with federated (SAML) authentication
questions.explanation: Client VPN supports certificate, Active Directory and SAML federated authentication and can give users access to private resources such as an RDS instance in a private subnet.

questions.prompt: A company needs a dedicated, private network connection between its data centre and AWS that gives consistent performance and does not traverse the public internet. What should it use?
choices: VPC peering
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet
An internet gateway
questions.correctChoice: AWS Direct Connect
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides dedicated network connections from on-premises to AWS with consistent bandwidth and latency characteristics.

questions.prompt: A company needs encrypted hybrid connectivity to AWS within a few days and has a modest budget. It can tolerate internet-based latency variation. Which option is most suitable?
choices: A VPC peering connection
A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint
A dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
questions.correctChoice: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
questions.explanation: A Site-to-Site VPN can be created in minutes over the internet at low cost. Direct Connect requires physical provisioning with a location or partner and has higher cost.

questions.prompt: A company uses Direct Connect to reach its VPCs. A new compliance rule requires IPsec encryption of all in-transit traffic between the data centre and AWS. Which approach satisfies this?
choices: Run a Site-to-Site VPN over the Direct Connect connection
Enable VPC Flow Logs on the Direct Connect virtual interface
Create a gateway endpoint for the traffic
Assume Direct Connect traffic is already encrypted with IPsec by default
questions.correctChoice: Run a Site-to-Site VPN over the Direct Connect connection
questions.explanation: Direct Connect is private but not IPsec-encrypted by default. An IPsec Site-to-Site VPN running over Direct Connect adds encryption.

questions.prompt: A company uses a Direct Connect connection as the primary link to its VPCs. The link is critical, but a second Direct Connect circuit is too expensive and slow to provision. What is the most cost-effective way to improve availability?
choices: Add a Site-to-Site VPN as a backup path over the internet
Use a gateway endpoint as the failover path
Replace Direct Connect with VPC peering
Add a second route table association to the subnets
questions.correctChoice: Add a Site-to-Site VPN as a backup path over the internet
questions.explanation: A Site-to-Site VPN is a quick, inexpensive backup that takes over if Direct Connect fails. The others do not provide hybrid connectivity.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Direct Connect charges is correct?
choices: Charges depend only on the number of VPCs connected to the connection
Port-hours are charged regardless of usage, outbound data transfer is charged and inbound transfer is free
Inbound and outbound data transfer are both charged at the same per-GB rate
Only data transferred is charged, and there is no charge for the provisioned port
questions.correctChoice: Port-hours are charged regardless of usage, outbound data transfer is charged and inbound transfer is free
questions.explanation: Direct Connect pricing includes port capacity and port-hours (regardless of usage) plus data transfer out. Data transfer in is free.

questions.prompt: A company needs only about 200 Mbps of dedicated connectivity and wants to obtain it through an AWS Direct Connect partner. Which connection type is appropriate?
choices: A transit gateway peering attachment
A Client VPN endpoint
A dedicated connection
A hosted connection
questions.correctChoice: A hosted connection
questions.explanation: Hosted connections are provisioned via APN partners at lower capacities (from 50 Mbps). Dedicated connections are physical ports of 1, 10, 100 or 400 Gbps.

questions.prompt: A company's Site-to-Site VPN to AWS suffers from variable latency over the public internet. It wants better performance without buying Direct Connect and without changing the IPsec-based approach. Which action fits?
choices: Replace the VPN with VPC peering between the VPC and the on-premises network
Attach the VPN to a virtual private gateway and enable Traffic Mirroring on the tunnels
Enable acceleration (AWS Global Accelerator) on a VPN connection attached to a transit gateway
Add a NAT gateway in the VPC in front of the customer gateway device to speed up traffic
questions.correctChoice: Enable acceleration (AWS Global Accelerator) on a VPN connection attached to a transit gateway
questions.explanation: Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN routes traffic over the AWS global network via Global Accelerator and is supported on VPN attachments to a transit gateway.

questions.prompt: What does VPC Flow Logs capture?
choices: Operating-system and application logs from instances in the VPC
Metadata about IP traffic to and from network interfaces: addresses, ports, protocol and accept or reject action
The full packet payloads of traffic flowing through the VPC's network interfaces
API calls made to VPC resources, including who made them and when
questions.correctChoice: Metadata about IP traffic to and from network interfaces: addresses, ports, protocol and accept or reject action
questions.explanation: Flow logs record metadata about IP traffic (addresses, ports, protocol, bytes, packets, action) but not payloads. API activity is recorded by CloudTrail.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to retain VPC Flow Logs cheaply for long-term analysis with a query service. Where should the logs be delivered?
choices: A Gateway Load Balancer
An EBS volume attached to a bastion
An Amazon S3 bucket
An Elastic IP address
questions.correctChoice: An Amazon S3 bucket
questions.explanation: Flow logs can be delivered to S3, CloudWatch Logs or Amazon Data Firehose. S3 is the low-cost option for retention and querying.

questions.prompt: A flow log for a web server's ENI shows inbound traffic on port 443 recorded as ACCEPT, but the return traffic to the client's ephemeral port is recorded as REJECT. The security group allows inbound 443. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The subnet's NACL outbound rules do not allow the ephemeral port range
The internet gateway is blocking stateful replies
The route table is missing a local route
The security group is missing an outbound rule for the ephemeral port range
questions.correctChoice: The subnet's NACL outbound rules do not allow the ephemeral port range
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful, so responses are not rejected by them. A stateless NACL without an outbound rule for the client's ephemeral ports rejects the reply.

questions.prompt: A security team needs copies of actual network packets from specific instances, forwarded to an intrusion detection appliance for analysis. Which feature should they use?
choices: A NAT gateway with logging enabled
VPC Traffic Mirroring
VPC Flow Logs
A security group rule that logs packets
questions.correctChoice: VPC Traffic Mirroring
questions.explanation: Traffic Mirroring copies packets (encapsulated with VXLAN) from a source ENI to a target for inspection. Flow logs capture only metadata.

questions.prompt: An application in a VPC must be restricted to making outbound HTTPS requests only to a list of approved domain names, with managed deep packet inspection at the VPC perimeter. Which service meets this?
choices: Security groups
Elastic IP addresses
Network ACLs
AWS Network Firewall
questions.correctChoice: AWS Network Firewall
questions.explanation: Network Firewall is a managed stateful firewall that can filter by domain name and protocol and perform deep packet inspection. Security groups and NACLs filter only by IP, port and protocol.

questions.prompt: A company needs intrusion prevention with custom Suricata-compatible rules for traffic entering and leaving a VPC. The team wants a managed, automatically scaling service and does not want to deploy or patch appliances. Which solution fits best?
choices: Network ACLs with high-numbered allow rules
Third-party firewall appliances on EC2 behind a Gateway Load Balancer
Security groups with deny rules for known-bad addresses
AWS Network Firewall
questions.correctChoice: AWS Network Firewall
questions.explanation: Network Firewall is managed, scales automatically, uses the open-source Suricata engine and provides IDS/IPS. GWLB-based appliances also work but add management overhead; SGs and NACLs cannot do deep inspection.

questions.prompt: Mirrored traffic from many instances must be sent to a scalable group of monitoring appliances rather than a single ENI. Which can be used as a Traffic Mirroring target?
choices: A UDP-enabled Network Load Balancer (or a Gateway Load Balancer)
A transit gateway attachment in the VPC
An Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener
An internet gateway attached to the VPC
questions.correctChoice: A UDP-enabled Network Load Balancer (or a Gateway Load Balancer)
questions.explanation: Traffic Mirroring targets can be an ENI, a UDP-enabled Network Load Balancer or a Gateway Load Balancer. ALBs do not accept the VXLAN/UDP mirrored traffic.

questions.prompt: A large VPC with many ENIs, interface endpoints and NAT gateways may approach its Network Address Usage (NAU) quota. How can the team track NAU proactively?
choices: Enable NAU monitoring on the VPC and use CloudWatch NAU metrics
Enable VPC Flow Logs and count the unique source addresses in the logs
Enable Traffic Mirroring on the VPC's ENIs and inspect the packet counts
Use AWS CloudTrail to count the API calls made against the VPC
questions.correctChoice: Enable NAU monitoring on the VPC and use CloudWatch NAU metrics
questions.explanation: NAU measures the resources in a VPC (e.g. ENI IPs, endpoints per AZ, NAT gateways). Once NAU monitoring is enabled on the VPC, CloudWatch metrics can be used to track it.

questions.prompt: A team needs SSH access to instances in private subnets. The instances have no public IP addresses, the team does not want to run bastion hosts, and the SSM Agent cannot be installed. Which option meets these needs?
choices: A NAT gateway with port forwarding to the instances
A bastion host with an Elastic IP in a public subnet
An EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint
An egress-only internet gateway
questions.correctChoice: An EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint
questions.explanation: EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint lets you connect to private instances without a bastion or public IPs and without needing the SSM Agent. NAT gateways and egress-only gateways do not allow inbound access.

questions.prompt: A team wants to capture IP traffic information only for one specific EC2 instance rather than an entire VPC. At which level can they create the flow log?
choices: The instance's network interface (ENI)
The route table of the instance's subnet
The internet gateway attached to the VPC
The security group attached to the instance
questions.correctChoice: The instance's network interface (ENI)
questions.explanation: Flow logs can be created for a VPC, a subnet or an individual ENI (and for transit gateways or attachments).

questions.prompt: A VPC has no internet gateway or NAT device. Workloads must privately reach Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, and a partner's service offered through AWS PrivateLink, at the lowest cost. Which combination should be used?
choices: A gateway endpoint for S3 and interface endpoints for SQS and the partner service
A gateway endpoint for SQS and interface endpoints for S3 and the partner service
Gateway endpoints for S3, SQS and the partner service
Interface endpoints for all three services
questions.correctChoice: A gateway endpoint for S3 and interface endpoints for SQS and the partner service
questions.explanation: S3 gateway endpoints are free; SQS and PrivateLink partner services are available only through interface endpoints (charged per hour and per GB).

questions.prompt: A company runs 20 VPCs, each with its own NAT gateways in several AZs, and NAT hourly charges are high. The VPCs are in one Region and need only outbound IPv4 internet access. Which design reduces cost while keeping connectivity?
choices: Replace the NAT gateways with interface endpoints in each VPC for internet destinations
Peer all VPCs with one VPC that has NAT gateways and route 0.0.0.0/0 through the peering
Attach the VPCs to a transit gateway and route 0.0.0.0/0 to a central egress VPC with NAT gateways
Route 0.0.0.0/0 in each VPC to a virtual private gateway attached to that VPC
questions.correctChoice: Attach the VPCs to a transit gateway and route 0.0.0.0/0 to a central egress VPC with NAT gateways
questions.explanation: A transit gateway lets many VPCs share a centralised egress VPC. VPC peering is not transitive, so peered VPCs cannot use another VPC's NAT gateway.

questions.prompt: A central security account runs a scalable fleet of third-party firewall appliances. Application VPCs in many accounts must have their traffic transparently inspected by this fleet. Which approach fits?
choices: Place a NAT gateway in each application VPC that forwards all traffic to the appliances
Peer each application VPC with the security VPC and route traffic to the appliances' IP addresses
Share the appliances' ENIs with each application account using AWS RAM and route to them
Expose the GWLB as an endpoint service, create a GWLB endpoint in each application VPC and route traffic to it
questions.correctChoice: Expose the GWLB as an endpoint service, create a GWLB endpoint in each application VPC and route traffic to it
questions.explanation: GWLB endpoints use PrivateLink to reach the GWLB in the provider VPC, which distributes flows across the appliances. Route table entries send traffic to the endpoint.

questions.prompt: Workloads in private subnets in two AZs call a partner API that allows traffic only from a small set of fixed public IP addresses. What is the best approach?
choices: Use an interface VPC endpoint for the partner's public API and give the partner its address
Use a public NAT gateway with an Elastic IP in each AZ and give the partner those addresses
Assign auto-assigned public IPv4 addresses to the instances and give the partner those addresses
Use an egress-only internet gateway and give the partner the gateway's address
questions.correctChoice: Use a public NAT gateway with an Elastic IP in each AZ and give the partner those addresses
questions.explanation: Public NAT gateways have static Elastic IPs and present them as the source address of outbound traffic. Auto-assigned public IPs change on stop/start.

questions.prompt: A team wants outbound internet access for private subnets in several AZs using a single NAT gateway resource that automatically spans AZs, without placing and maintaining a NAT gateway in a public subnet for each AZ. Which option fits?
choices: A zonal NAT gateway in one AZ
A regional NAT gateway
A NAT instance in an Auto Scaling group
A private NAT gateway
questions.correctChoice: A regional NAT gateway
questions.explanation: A regional NAT gateway spans AZs automatically and does not require a public subnet, providing public connectivity. Zonal NAT gateways are tied to one AZ.

questions.prompt: Private subnets have no internet gateway or NAT, and policy forbids adding them. Administrators still need to use Systems Manager Session Manager to reach the instances. What must be added?
choices: A virtual private gateway attached to the VPC
Interface VPC endpoints for the Systems Manager services
An Elastic IP on each instance
A gateway VPC endpoint for Systems Manager
questions.correctChoice: Interface VPC endpoints for the Systems Manager services
questions.explanation: Systems Manager is reached privately via interface endpoints (PrivateLink); gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.prompt: A company moves tens of terabytes a month from AWS to its data centre on a steady basis. Internet data-transfer-out charges are high and performance consistency matters. Which solution is most appropriate?
choices: A NAT gateway in a public subnet
AWS Direct Connect
A Site-to-Site VPN over the internet
VPC peering to the on-premises network
questions.correctChoice: AWS Direct Connect
questions.explanation: Direct Connect reduces network costs for sustained large transfers (lower data-transfer-out rates) and provides consistent throughput. VPN traffic is charged at internet transfer rates.

questions.prompt: A web server's security group allows inbound TCP 443 from anywhere, and an engineer removes every outbound rule from it. The NACLs allow all traffic. What is the effect?
choices: Nothing changes, because security groups ignore outbound rules by default
The server can initiate outbound connections, but inbound HTTPS connections fail
Clients cannot connect because responses are blocked by the missing outbound rule
Clients can still connect and get responses, but the server cannot start new outbound connections
questions.correctChoice: Clients can still connect and get responses, but the server cannot start new outbound connections
questions.explanation: Because security groups are stateful, replies to allowed inbound connections are returned automatically. With no outbound rules, new connections initiated by the instance are denied.

questions.prompt: To give database-tier instances internet access for patches, an engineer adds a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway in their private subnet's route table. The instances have only private IPv4 addresses and still cannot reach the internet. What is the correct fix?
choices: Replace the IGW route with a route to an egress-only internet gateway
Remove the IGW route and route 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT gateway in a public subnet
Attach a second internet gateway to the VPC
Associate the subnet with the main route table
questions.correctChoice: Remove the IGW route and route 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT gateway in a public subnet
questions.explanation: An IGW performs translation only for instances that have a public or Elastic IPv4 address. Keeping instances private requires a NAT gateway in a public subnet. An egress-only IGW is for IPv6.

questions.prompt: Two VPCs in the same Region exchange tens of terabytes of data each month. The company wants the lowest-cost private connectivity with no bandwidth bottleneck between them. No other VPCs are involved. Which option is best?
choices: VPC peering
An AWS PrivateLink endpoint service in front of each VPC
A transit gateway with an attachment from each VPC
A Site-to-Site VPN between the two VPCs
questions.correctChoice: VPC peering
questions.explanation: Peering has no hourly charge and no bandwidth bottleneck, so it is cheapest for two VPCs. Transit gateways add hourly and per-GB charges, and VPN tunnels have limited throughput.

questions.prompt: A central network team wants to control subnets, route tables and gateways, while 12 workload accounts in the same AWS Organization launch their own EC2 instances into those same subnets without VPC peering. Which approach should they take?
choices: Share the default subnets of the network account's default VPC with the workload accounts using RAM and route tables
Create a VPC peering connection between each workload account's own VPC and the network account's VPC and manage routes centrally
Enable RAM sharing in the organization and share non-default subnets of the network account's VPC with workload accounts
Create a transit gateway and attach every workload account's VPC to it
questions.correctChoice: Enable RAM sharing in the organization and share non-default subnets of the network account's VPC with workload accounts
questions.explanation: VPC sharing via RAM shares subnets within an Organization; participants manage only their own resources. Default subnets cannot be shared, and peering or transit gateways connect separate VPCs rather than sharing subnets.

questions.prompt: For forensic analysis, a security team needs full packet captures from a production instance. They cannot install agents or change software on the instance and want minimal impact on it. Which solution fits?
choices: Enable VPC Flow Logs with the ALL filter on the instance's ENI
Enable AWS Network Firewall alert logging for the VPC
Configure VPC Traffic Mirroring from the instance's ENI to a monitoring target
Install a packet-capture tool on the instance and ship the files to S3
questions.correctChoice: Configure VPC Traffic Mirroring from the instance's ENI to a monitoring target
questions.explanation: Traffic Mirroring copies packets at the ENI level without touching the instance. Flow logs record only metadata, not packet contents.

questions.prompt: Dual-stack instances in private subnets must reach both IPv4 and IPv6 internet destinations but must not accept connections initiated from the internet. Which route table configuration meets this?
choices: 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 both to an internet gateway
0.0.0.0/0 to an egress-only internet gateway and ::/0 to a NAT gateway
0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 both to a NAT gateway
0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT gateway and ::/0 to an egress-only internet gateway
questions.correctChoice: 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT gateway and ::/0 to an egress-only internet gateway
questions.explanation: NAT gateways handle outbound IPv4 and egress-only internet gateways handle outbound-only IPv6. An internet gateway would permit inbound connections.

questions.prompt: Remote engineers and finance staff must connect from their laptops. Engineers need access to the application subnets, finance staff to a reporting subnet only. The company already uses Active Directory. Which solution gives least-privilege access with the least overhead?
choices: A Site-to-Site VPN with a customer gateway on each user's laptop
AWS Client VPN with Active Directory authentication and authorization rules per AD group
A bastion host with a shared SSH key and a public IP address
A single Client VPN certificate shared by all users with one security group
questions.correctChoice: AWS Client VPN with Active Directory authentication and authorization rules per AD group
questions.explanation: Client VPN supports AD authentication, and AD groups or security groups provide granular, per-user-group network access. Site-to-Site VPN is for networks, not individual users.

questions.prompt: A web server's security group allows inbound HTTPS only from 198.51.100.0/24 and 192.0.2.0/24. Its subnet's NACL has inbound rule 100 DENY all from 192.0.2.0/24 and rule 110 ALLOW all from 0.0.0.0/0 (outbound allows all). Which clients can connect over HTTPS?
choices: Clients from any address, because the NACL allows all traffic
Only clients in 198.51.100.0/24
Only clients in 192.0.2.0/24
questions.correctChoice: Only clients in 198.51.100.0/24
questions.explanation: Traffic must be permitted by both the NACL and the security group. The NACL denies 192.0.2.0/24 and the security group rejects other sources, so only 198.51.100.0/24 passes.

questions.prompt: A service currently runs on EC2 instances. A new version is built on AWS Lambda and traffic must shift gradually (for example 10% then 50%) between the two across accounts without changing clients. Which solution fits?
choices: A VPC Lattice service whose listener rule weights traffic between an EC2 and a Lambda target group
A VPC peering connection between the accounts, using weighted route table entries
A transit gateway route table with equal-cost routes to each version of the service
A Gateway Load Balancer with two GWLB endpoints, one for each version of the service
questions.correctChoice: A VPC Lattice service whose listener rule weights traffic between an EC2 and a Lambda target group
questions.explanation: VPC Lattice target groups can hold EC2, IP, Lambda or ALB targets, and listener rules can weight traffic for blue/green or canary deployments.

questions.prompt: A company needs sustained private connectivity of about 10 Gbps from its data centre to AWS. A Site-to-Site VPN tunnel supports up to about 1.25 Gbps. Which option meets the throughput requirement with dependable performance?
choices: A dedicated 10 Gbps Direct Connect connection
An AWS Client VPN endpoint with certificate-based authentication
A VPC peering connection between the VPC and the data centre network
A single Site-to-Site VPN connection using one IPsec tunnel
questions.correctChoice: A dedicated 10 Gbps Direct Connect connection
questions.explanation: Dedicated Direct Connect connections are available at 1, 10, 100 and 400 Gbps with consistent performance. A VPN tunnel is capped near 1.25 Gbps.
